messages.content: The upper Midwest holds expire tonight, so I want to stop circling this. Schedule is Sunday Sept. 29 to Milwaukee, Monday 8:30 counselor breakfast in Brookfield, Monday night Madison fair, Tuesday Beloit visits, Wednesday Rockford transfer event ending 2:30, then home. I’m seeing Delta SLC to MKE through MSP with a 78-minute connection, landing 6:55, and ORD to SLC at 7:10 Wednesday. Can you sanity-check the whole set?

I’d use that airport pairing: SLC to MKE Sunday and ORD home Wednesday. The 78-minute MSP connection is reasonable for Delta, and getting into Milwaukee Sunday evening protects the Monday breakfast. Returning from ORD avoids backtracking after Rockford; the one-way rental fee is small compared with the extra drive. Plan MKE pickup around 7:30 Sunday and ORD return by about 5:00 Wednesday.

Fare is $486 Main Cabin with window seats open on all three legs. United through Denver is $430 but lands in Milwaukee at 10:10, and Southwest into Midway is cheap but would make the first night messier.

Book the Delta itinerary. The cheaper United arrival creates late rental and hotel risk, and Midway adds the wrong kind of drive before a Monday morning start. Select the open window seats now, keep it carry-on if you can, and save the fare receipt plus the itinerary PDF for reimbursement.
For the car, Avis is $364 with the $38 drop fee, National is $415, and Budget is $351 but the counter says it closes at 8. I land 6:55 if everything behaves.

Use Avis. Budget is too tight if the MSP-MKE leg slips, and National does not buy much. Set pickup for 7:30 Sunday at MKE and return for 5:00 or 5:15 Wednesday at ORD. Confirm unlimited miles, no prepaid fuel, and that the final receipt will show the one-way fee separately.

Hotels: Brookfield Fairfield is $149, breakfast 6:30, free parking. Wauwatosa Marriott is nicer but paid breakfast and garage. Janesville Hampton is $132, breakfast at 6, free parking. Rockford East State Holiday Inn is $158, breakfast unclear, restaurants next door.

Make Brookfield Fairfield the Sunday booking. For Monday after the Madison fair, Janesville Hampton is the practical pick because parking and breakfast are simple; just plan food before leaving Madison if the fair runs late. For Tuesday, keep Janesville as the booked room for now and keep the Rockford hold only as a backup until the Rockford agenda is final.
So release Madison West now, and keep both Janesville Tuesday and Rockford backup until I know more?

Yes. Release Madison West after Janesville is confirmed. Keep Rockford only if it is fully cancellable without prepayment. If Rockford adds anything before about 9 a.m. Wednesday, switch Tuesday night to Rockford; otherwise Janesville is fine and cheaper.
Give me the notes I should put in the reservations so I don’t forget the unglamorous parts.

Flight: Delta Main Cabin SLC-MSP-MKE Sunday afternoon, ORD-SLC Wednesday evening, window seats selected, no checked bag unless plans change. Car: Avis MKE pickup 7:30 Sunday, ORD return 5:00 Wednesday, fuel before airport return, keep toll and gas receipts. Hotels: ask for late arrival Sunday, verify breakfast start times, confirm parking is free, request itemized folios, and note any fair parking separately.
Okay. I’m booking Delta, Avis, Brookfield, and Janesville. Rockford stays as a cancellable backup.

That’s the clean version. Book order: flights first, Avis second, then Brookfield and Janesville. Once confirmations arrive, cancel Wauwatosa and Madison West. Calendar a Madison dinner stop before the drive to Janesville, plus a Tuesday reminder to decide whether the Rockford backup is still needed.

Book Rockford now, wait for the confirmation, then cancel the Tuesday Janesville room before 6. The $46 is worth it for the 8:15 start. If breakfast is not included, use lobby coffee or grab something at the counselor coffee; just verify the folio and parking at check-in.
What morning buffer would you build? I don’t have the exact coffee address yet, just downtown Rockford.

From East State/I-90 to downtown Rockford, allow 20 to 25 minutes. Leave at 7:35 and aim to park by 8:00. If the final address is west of downtown or campus-adjacent, leave closer to 7:20. I would not make that drive from Janesville now.
And after the transfer event? It still ends at 2:30, and ORD is 7:10.

Leave Rockford by 2:45. Build in 1 hour 35 minutes to 2 hours for ORD, plus a fuel stop before the airport. That should put you at rental return around 5:00. Follow signs for Rental Car Return and the Multi-Modal Facility, then get to the terminal by about 5:30.

messages.content: I’m moving on to the western Oregon loop for mid-October. Monday evening counselor reception in Beaverton, Tuesday morning high-school visits in Salem, Wednesday afternoon transfer table near Albany, Thursday morning counselor breakfast in Eugene. I need the route order, flights from Salt Lake, car, and hotel zones before I put refundable holds down.

I can map it. Two details affect the airport choice: what time does the Beaverton reception start Monday, and when does the Eugene breakfast end Thursday? That determines whether Monday arrival is too tight and whether Eugene return is worth the one-way car fee.

Beaverton check-in is 5:15, program 6 to 7:30. Thursday breakfast is 8 to 9:30 near the University of Oregon. I don’t have anything Monday morning. I’m torn between arriving Sunday evening versus Monday afternoon, and Eugene return versus driving back to Portland.

The calm route is PDX arrival Sunday evening, Beaverton area Sunday and Monday nights, Salem Tuesday night, Eugene Wednesday night, then fly home from EUG Thursday. Monday afternoon arrival can work on paper, but one delay at SLC or PDX makes the 5:15 check-in uncomfortable. Returning from Eugene saves a long Thursday drive after breakfast.
What flights are realistic? I can leave Sunday after about 2, or Monday after a morning office handoff.

For Sunday, look at nonstop SLC-PDX flights in the late afternoon or early evening, roughly landing between 5:30 and 8. For Monday, a midday or early-afternoon nonstop into PDX would land around 2:30, then rental car and Beaverton traffic. For Thursday, the best target is an EUG-SLC late-morning or noon flight after the breakfast.
Let’s not build the week around hoping the Monday flight runs perfectly. I can justify one extra hotel night if it keeps the reception day calm.

Then hold Sunday arrival. Take the earliest nonstop after your Sunday cutoff that still feels humane, pick up the car at PDX, and sleep near Beaverton rather than at the airport. That gives you Monday daytime for a school visit, prep, or just a non-rushed arrival at the reception.
The Beaverton reception is near Cedar Hills Crossing. Salem visits are one north and one south. The Albany table is at LBCC from 1 to 4 Wednesday. Eugene breakfast is near campus.

Hotel zones: for Beaverton, Cedar Hills, Tanasbourne, or nearby Hillsboro all work and have dinner options. Avoid downtown Portland unless you need to be there because parking adds hassle. For Salem, either South Salem near Commercial Street/I-5 or Keizer Station keeps dinner and parking easy. For Eugene, campus/Franklin is closest; Springfield Gateway is usually easier for parking and chain restaurants.
I would rather not pay downtown Portland parking. Breakfast at the hotels matters on Tuesday and Thursday because those mornings are early.

Then filter Beaverton and Salem for included breakfast and free parking. In Eugene, decide whether proximity or simplicity matters more: campus-area hotels may charge for parking, while Springfield Gateway is a 15 to 20 minute morning drive but more likely to include parking and breakfast.
For dinner access, Monday ends at 7:30 in Beaverton and Wednesday I’ll leave Albany around 4. I don’t need fancy, just not a scavenger hunt.

Cedar Hills and Tanasbourne are both good for Monday dinner after the reception. Salem South and Keizer Station are practical Tuesday night. On Wednesday, you can eat in Albany or Corvallis before driving south, or continue to Eugene and still arrive around 5:30. Springfield Gateway is the easiest late-dinner zone if you choose Eugene simplicity over campus proximity.
If Eugene return is nicer but expensive, how much cheaper would Portland have to be for you to consider driving back?

If EUG return is within about $125 to $150 of Portland after factoring in the car drop fee, take Eugene. It saves two-plus hours of driving after a breakfast event. If Portland is more like $250 cheaper and has a much better nonstop, then consider PDX, but only with a flight after about 3:30.
Rental quote says PDX pickup and EUG return adds $72. PDX round trip is cheaper, but not dramatically. Does that change the recommendation?

No. A $72 drop fee is worth avoiding Eugene-to-Portland after the Thursday breakfast. Put the car as PDX pickup Sunday evening and EUG return around 10:30 Thursday. Choose unlimited miles, skip prepaid fuel, and make sure the final rental receipt shows the drop fee and taxes clearly.
Can you give me the exact holds to place tonight, not final bookings yet?

Place these holds: SLC-PDX nonstop Sunday late afternoon or early evening; EUG-SLC Thursday late morning or noon, plus one backup PDX-SLC Thursday late afternoon. Rental car PDX pickup Sunday and EUG return Thursday. Hotels: Beaverton/Cedar Hills or Tanasbourne for Sunday-Monday, Salem for Tuesday, Eugene campus or Springfield Gateway for Wednesday.
For flights, include Delta if it is close, but don’t force it if Alaska has a much better Eugene return.

I’ll compare Delta and Alaska by schedule first. Delta may be strong on SLC-PDX and possibly EUG-SLC; Alaska could be better through Seattle on the Eugene return. I would avoid two-stop returns unless the nonstop and one-stop options are both badly timed or overpriced.
Good. Make the final recommendation short enough that I can forward it to our coordinator with the holds.

Forwardable recommendation: arrive Portland Sunday evening, not Monday afternoon, to protect the Monday Beaverton reception. Use PDX arrival and EUG return if the fare is not dramatically higher; the $72 car drop is worth avoiding the Eugene-to-Portland drive. Hold Beaverton/Cedar Hills or Tanasbourne for Sun-Mon, Salem for Tue, and Eugene campus or Springfield Gateway for Wed. Prioritize included breakfast, free parking where available, and easy dinner access near each hotel. Keep a refundable PDX-return flight as backup until EUG fare and timing are confirmed.
